notes: absuelto, declarar inocente
definition: To clear of guilt or blame; exonerate.
example: Our dog, Rufus, was absolved of stealing Mom's glasses when they were found safe in her purse.

notes: firme / tajante, no da su brazo a torcer
definition: Not giving in; stubborn; firm.
example: Ron is adamant about not changing plans. He insists we should still camp out even though the weather report now says it will be cold and rainy.

notes: amable, de buen carácter
definition: Good-natured; friendly and pleasant.
example: My amiable dog greets both strangers and old friends with a happy yip and energetic tail-wagging.

notes: carente de principios éticos o morales
definition: Lacking a sense of right and wrong; without moral principles.
example: Jerry is almost totally amoral. He cares only about making money and having fun and couldn't care less about right or wrong.

notes: hostil / enemistad, fuerte desagrado
definition: Strong dislike; bitter hostility; hatred.
example: The animosity between fans of the soccer teams was so strong that fights broke out all over the stadium.

notes: enemigo, rival, oponente
definition: An opponent; one who opposes or competes with another.
example: At the divorce hearing, the husband and wife were such bitter antagonists that it was hard to believe they had once loved each other.

notes: excéntrico, diferente a lo común
definition: Differing from what is customary; odd; unusual.
example: Bruce is quite eccentric. For example, he lives in a circular house and rides to work on a motorcycle, in a three-piece suit.

notes: encontrar, reunión inesperada
definition: A brief or an unexpected meeting; to meet unexpectedly.
example: My encounter with Malik in a Los Angeles supermarket surprised me, since I thought he still lived in Chicago.

notes: epítome, modelo ideal de algo
definition: A perfect or typical example of a general quality or type.
example: To many, the epitome of cuteness is a furry, round-eyed puppy.

notes: malignar / hablar mal de, dañar reputación
definition: To speak evil of; tell lies about; defame.
example: That vicious Hollywood reporter often maligns movie stars, forever damaging their public images.

notes: brusco / seco / cortante al hablar
definition: Rudely brief when speaking to someone; abrupt.
example: The fast-food manager trained workers to give polite, full answers to customers, not curt responses.

notes: bajar el ánimo, quitar la esperanza o motivación
definition: To lower the spirits of; weaken the confidence or cheerfulness of.
example: Cara's refusal to date my brother demoralized him so completely that for months, he lacked the confidence to ask another woman out.

notes: elección difícil entre dos opciones no deseadas
definition: A situation requiring a difficult choice between two undesirable alternatives.
example: The store manager faced a dilemma: either having a needy elderly man arrested or ignoring store rules about shoplifters.

notes: preferencia o tendencia a actuar de cierta forma
definition: A tendency, or preference, to think, act, or behave in a certain way; a leaning.
example: My inclination is to major in nursing, but I'm going to speak to a few nurses before I make my final decision.

notes: enojado, furioso, muy enfadado
definition: Very angry; furious.
example: If Kate got angry only occasionally, I could take her more seriously, but she's always irate about something or other.

notes: respondió de manera rápida, cortante o ingeniosa
definition: To reply, especially in a quick, sharp, or witty way.
example: When I told my parents I'd put the dishes in the dishwasher the next morning, my father retorted, "Maybe we should serve you dinner in the mornings, too."

notes: arruinar / impedir / dañar intencionalmente
definition: To deliberately destroy or damage other people's work or property.
example: A fired programmer sabotaged the company's network by infecting it with a computer virus.

notes: subsecuente, que sigue en orden o tiempo
definition: Following, in time or order; next; later.
example: The first few times Janet drove on a highway, she was terrified, but on subsequent trips, she felt more relaxed.

notes: cauteloso / desconfiado, estar alerta
definition: Cautious; on guard; suspicious.
example: "There's no such thing as a free lunch" means that we should be wary about promises of getting something for nothing.

notes: entusiasmo / fervor / pasión por una causa (zealot)
definition: Enthusiastic devotion to a purpose, cause, or ideal; passion.
example: Velma attacked her food with such zeal that I thought she hadn't eaten for a week!

notes: aclamación, elogio público entusiasta
definition: Praise; enthusiastic and public approval.
example: Any subway system that is clean, quiet, and safe deserves acclaim.

notes: adyacente, cercano, al lado de
definition: Close; in contact with; bordering; neighboring.
example: If you keep your dishes in a cupboard that's adjacent to the dishwasher, you won't have to walk too far when putting away the clean dishes.

notes: provocar o hacer que alguien te dé una respuesta o atención
definition: To bring out; evoke; draw forth.
example: The basketball player's three-point shot to win the game in its final seconds elicited a roar of delight from the excited fans.

notes: absorber / ocupar completamente la atención
definition: To hold the interest of; occupy the complete attention of.
example: The suspenseful TV movie so engrossed Bryan that he didn't even budge when he was called to dinner.

notes: escalar / aumentar / intensificar rápidamente
definition: To expand; increase or intensify rapidly.
example: The fight between the two hockey players escalated into an all-out battle among members of both teams.

notes: explotar / aprovecharse egoístamente de algo o alguien
definition: To take advantage of; use selfishly or unethically.
example: At the turn of the century, factory owners exploited children by making them work in terrible conditions for as many as eighteen hours a day.

notes: metódico / sistemático / ordenado en procedimientos
definition: Orderly; systematic; done according to a systematic procedure.
example: Juanita is so methodical about her diet that she classifies the foods in each meal into different nutritional categories.

notes: obsoleto / anticuado / fuera de uso
definition: Out-of-date; no longer in active use or practice.
example: Smartphones are so common now that they have made pagers obsolete.

notes: tangible / concreto / palpable, que se puede percibir
definition: Solid; real; capable of being touched or felt.
example: The sculptor loved making her ideas tangible by giving them form in metal and stone.

notes: terminar / finalizar / poner fin a algo
definition: To end; bring to a conclusion.
example: As the clock's hands inched toward 3:00, the students waited impatiently for the bell to terminate the last class before spring vacation.

notes: enfermedad / debilidad física / discapacidad
definition: A physical weakness or defect; ailment; disability.
example: Rick uses a wheelchair, but he doesn't let his infirmity keep him from traveling.

notes: revitalizar / nueva vida / dar nueva energía
definition: To renew the strength and energy of; restore to a vigorous, active condition.
example: When DeShawn is tired after work, he finds a brief nap revitalizes him for an evening out with friends.

notes: escaso / disperso / poco abundante
definition: Distributed thinly; not thick or crowded; thin.
example: There are thick pine forests at the foot of the mountain, but higher up, the trees become sparse.

notes: violar un derecho o una regla / interferir
definition: To actively break the terms of a law or agreement; to interfere with.
example: The protesters may picket the nuclear power plant as long as they don't infringe on other people's right to enter and exit freely.

notes: innovación, algo nuevo o método revolucionario
definition: A new method, idea, or product; something new.
example: When commercial bakers first offered sliced bread, it was considered an exciting innovation.

notes: desigualdad / falta de equidad / injusticia
definition: Lack of fairness or justice; an unfair circumstance or action; injustice.
example: In South Africa, Mahatma Gandhi experienced an inequity that was all too common at the time—he was thrown off a "whites only" train.

notes: disuasivo / desaliento / evita que algo suceda
definition: A thing that discourages or prevents someone from doing something; a prevention.
example: As a deterrent to burglars, my father put a sign on our lawn that says, "Beware of pit bull."

notes: subjetivo, basado en sentimientos personales
definition: Based on or influenced by personal feelings, tastes, or opinions; one-sided.
example: Martina, a highly subjective judge of her son's abilities, feels he's brilliant in every respect.

notes: conciso / breve y claro / directo al grano
definition: Briefly and clearly expressed; concise and to the point.
example: Text messages are usually succinct. People don't want to type any more words than necessary to get their messages across.

notes: implicación / consecuencia / algo sugerido
definition: A conclusion that can be drawn from something; something suggested.
example: When the boss said that company profits were down, the implication was that nobody would be getting a raise.

notes: arbitrario, determinado por capricho o impulso
definition: Determined by personal judgment, not rule or reason; based on impulse.
example: His choice of clothing seemed completely arbitrary.

notes: estafador / avaro, motivado por dinero
definition: Motivated only by financial gain; greedy.
example: Ed is totally mercenary. His philosophy is, "Pay me enough, and I'll do anything."

notes: alusión, mención sutil o sugerencia
definition: An indirect reference.
example: The author made a subtle allusion to classical mythology in the opening chapter.

notes: síndrome, grupo típico de síntomas
definition: A group of symptoms typical of a particular disease or condition.
example: Jet lag is a syndrome resulting from flying long distances; it often includes exhaustion, headache, and loss of appetite.

notes: eufemismo, término suave para no ofender
definition: A mild or vague term used as a substitute for one considered offensive or unpleasant.
example: 'Passed away' is a widely used euphemism for 'died'.

notes: apaciguar / calmar, ceder ante demandas
definition: To calm, especially by giving in to the demands of.
example: He tried to appease his angry boss by offering a quick solution.

notes: banal / trillado, carente de originalidad
definition: Lacking originality; overused; commonplace.
example: The movie had a banal plot that offered no surprises to the audience.

notes: manchar / perjudicar / afectar reputación o pureza
definition: To stain the honor of someone or something; to corrupt or damage.
example: The government scandal tainted the reputations of everyone involved.

notes: atacar / agredir / asaltar física o verbalmente
definition: To attack physically or verbally.
example: The critics assailed the new legislation with harsh insults.

notes: altruista, generoso, preocupado por los demás
definition: Unselfishly concerned for the welfare of others; unselfish.
example: Her altruistic work with community clinics inspired many young doctors.

notes: benigno / de buen carácter, bondadoso
definition: Kindly; gentle.
example: Finding a stranger on our doorstep startled me, but the benign expression on his face told me not to worry.

notes: aburrido / hastiado, indiferente por repetición
definition: Unexcited or bored about something already experienced repeatedly.
example: The new staff members were enthusiastic at the weekly meetings, but the old-timers were pretty blasé.

notes: comprender / constar de / abarcar
definition: To consist of; include.
example: The United Kingdom comprises England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

notes: condescender / rebajarse a hacer algo inferior
definition: To do something one feels is beneath oneself.
example: The snobby millionaire wouldn't condescend to associate with anyone who wasn't also rich.

notes: fachada / frente de un edificio o apariencia falsa
definition: The front of a building; also, a deceptive outward appearance.
example: The facade of the old department store was cleaned this summer. Now the store's brick front is an inviting bright orange-red.

translation: de labia fácil, elocuente pero falso, superficial
notes: labia / habla fluida pero falsa o superficial
definition: Characterized by a smooth, easy manner of speaking that often suggests insincerity or thoughtlessness.
example: Always ready with a slick promise, the glib politician smoothly talked his way into being re-elected.

notes: arrogante / altivo, mira a otros por encima del hombro
definition: Proud of one's appearance or accomplishments to the point of looking down on others; arrogant.
example: The Smiths acted as though they were better than anybody else. Not surprisingly, their haughty manner made them unpopular with their neighbors.

notes: difamación / calumnia por escrito (demandar)
definition: The publishing of false information that harms a person's reputation.
example: When Nick saw his name listed in the article as a gang member, he was furious. "That's libel!" he yelled. "How dare they print such a lie about me?"

notes: seudónimo / nombre falso de autor
definition: A false name used by an author; a pen name.
example: Samuel Langhorne Clemens wasn't the first author to use the pseudonym Mark Twain. A newspaper writer of the time used the same pen name.

notes: redundante / repetitivo, palabras innecesarias
definition: Wordy or needlessly repetitive.
example: The TV ad for a headache medicine was so redundant that it gave me a headache! The name of the product was repeated at least a dozen times.

notes: averse to / opuesto a, reacio a hacer algo
definition: Having a strong feeling of opposition or dislike; strongly opposed.
example: I'm averse to speaking in public because I don't enjoy making a fool of myself.

notes: detract from / restar importancia, valor o atractivo
definition: To take away from a particular value or quality; lessen.
example: People talking in a movie theater greatly detract from the enjoyment of watching a film.

notes: look at with disdain / sentimiento de desprecio o superioridad
definition: A feeling of contempt or scorn for someone or something regarded as unworthy.
example: Vinnie's repeated boasts about his muscle-building backfired. They caused his date to look at him with disdain, not admiration.

notes: revelar o dar a conocer un secreto
definition: To make known or reveal something private or secret.
example: Never trust Esta with a secret. She'll divulge it the minute you turn your back.

notes: gran felicidad, entusiasmo o júbilo
definition: Great happiness and exhilaration; a state of extreme joy.
example: When he received the college scholarship, my brother felt such elation that he wept with joy.

notes: endow with / dotar de una cualidad o talento
definition: To provide naturally with a quality, ability, or asset.
example: The American water shrew is endowed with feet that have air pockets, enabling the small animal to walk on water.

notes: acción de expulsar o forzar a alguien a salir
definition: The act of forcing someone to leave a place or organization.
example: Russian athletes faced expulsion from the Olympics when it was revealed that many were taking illegal drugs to improve their performance.

notes: muy avergonzado o humillado públicamente
definition: Deeply embarrassed, humiliated, or ashamed.
example: The reporter was mortified when he learned that he had delivered much of his news story facing away from the TV camera.

notes: anular / dejar sin validez o efecto legal
definition: Canceled; legally invalidated or made ineffective.
example: The results of the mayoral election were nullified after the townspeople found evidence of voting fraud.

notes: amenazante / señal de que algo malo va a pasar
definition: Threatening harm; giving the impression that something bad is going to happen.
example: Because of the dark, ominous storm clouds, we canceled the softball game.
